_doc: What each document says about itself (title page or cover as saved) and reading notes of the nps-landscape task. Filled in from the saved text or the page image; a field is left out where the document does not state it.

NPS-CLI-PCB.title: Cultural Landscapes Inventory: Pickett's Charge Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park
NPS-CLI-PCB.author: National Park Service
NPS-CLI-PCB.from: PDF p. 1 (cover: 'National Park Service / Cultural Landscapes Inventory / 2024 / Pickett's Charge Battlefield')
NPS-CLI-PCB.text_quality: born-digital text, clean; a line-end hyphen is dropped by the extraction in a few words (e.g. 'fenceenclosed')
NPS-CLI-PCB.covers: Codori, Henry Spangler, Staub, Sherfy, Rogers, Wentz, Bliss, McMillan, Pitzer farms; Seminary Ridge woodlots; fields, orchards, stone walls, fences, buildings, monuments of the Pickett's Charge field
NPS-CLI-PCB.state_dates_note: Mixed and dated in the text: 1863 conditions (physical history, pp. 48-51, and the 'at the time of the battle' sentences of the feature entries), commemorative-era features (1884-1933), and present conditions as surveyed for the 2024 inventory. Wall dimensions are present-day measurements. Fences are reconstructions of 1999-2012; orchards are replantings of 1984-2013.

NPS-CLI-ERR.title: Cultural Landscapes Inventory: Emmitsburg Road Ridge Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park
NPS-CLI-ERR.author: National Park Service
NPS-CLI-ERR.from: PDF p. 1 (cover: 'National Park Service / Cultural Landscapes Inventory / 2024 / Emmitsburg Road Ridge Battlefield')
NPS-CLI-ERR.text_quality: born-digital text, clean; a line-end hyphen is dropped by the extraction in a few words (e.g. 'CodoriTrostle')
NPS-CLI-ERR.covers: Klingel farm, parts of the Trostle and Codori farms, Neinstedt field; Codori-Trostle thicket, orchards, fences, stone walls, buildings, monuments
NPS-CLI-ERR.state_dates_note: Dated period by period in the text: 'Battle Period' / 'Battlefield Period' paragraphs describe July 1863 (drawn from the park's 2000 draft and 2002 Cultural Landscape Report for Emmitsburg Road Ridge); GBMA 1864-1895; park commission 1895-1927; 1930s; existing conditions about 2000 and 2024. Wall dimensions are present-day measurements; orchards were replanted in 2005 and 2009; fences rebuilt 2000-2012.

NPS-CLR-1STDAY.title: Cultural Landscape Report for First Day - Union 1st Corps Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park
NPS-CLR-1STDAY.author: John Auwaerter (Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, National Park Service, with the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry)
NPS-CLR-1STDAY.from: PDF p. 4 (Library of Congress cataloguing-in-publication data as saved: LCCN 2021035264; report by John Auwaerter, SUNY ESF; issued by the Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, Boston)
NPS-CLR-1STDAY.text_quality: two-column report with floating captions: the standard reading-order text interleaves columns, so quotes are cut from the content-stream-order text (tmp/library/web/nps/NPS-CLR-1STDAY/NPS-CLR-1STDAY.raw.txt, pdftotext -raw, line-end hyphenation repaired by scripts/build_extracts.py dehyphenate); born-digital text, clean
NPS-CLR-1STDAY.state_dates_note: Site history chapter (PDF pp. 31-68) describes the landscape by period: to July 1863 (battle-era farms, fields, fences, woods), GBMA 1863-1895, War Department 1895-1933, NPS 1933-2019. Existing-conditions and treatment chapters describe 2019-2021 conditions and reconstructions: never an 1863 profile.
NPS-CLR-1STDAY.covers: First Day field northwest of Gettysburg: Seminary campus, Thompson and Dustman lots, Schmucker, Herbst, McPherson, Forney, Wills, McClean, Harman, Herr, Sweney, Crist and Wisler farms; fields, fences, woodlots, orchards, roads, railroad grade, buildings; commemorative park features

NPS-TPG-COMMEM.title: Treatment Philosophy and Guidelines for the Battlefield Commemorative Area, Gettysburg National Military Park
NPS-TPG-COMMEM.author: John Auwaerter (State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry; Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, National Park Service, Boston)
NPS-TPG-COMMEM.from: PDF pp. 3-4 (title page: By John Auwaerter, SUNY ESF, Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, National Park Service; Library of Congress Control Number 2025937949; ETIC report GETT 305/196856A)
NPS-TPG-COMMEM.text_quality: two-column report: quotes are cut from the content-stream-order text (NPS-TPG-COMMEM.raw.txt, pdftotext -raw, line-end hyphenation repaired). The text layer lost the i of every fi ligature and one f of ff (battlefeld, felds, fg., diferent), so quotes are typed in the corrected spelling and matched letter for letter with those groups ignored (quote_mode cleaned; the raw excerpt is stored next to the quote)
NPS-TPG-COMMEM.state_dates_note: The Historical Overview (PDF pp. 33-45) dates each commemorative feature (1864-1938): those are features placed AFTER July 1863. The guidelines describe 2019-2023 condition and treatment. Statements about the 1863 battlefield (vernacular rail fences, 1863 public roads) are marked as such.
NPS-TPG-COMMEM.covers: Commemorative Area: GBMA 1864-1895, Park Commission 1895-1922, War Department to 1933; military avenues, monuments, observation towers, avenue fences, rebuilt earthworks, shell stones, iron tablets

NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.title: Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Military Park: Record of Treatment, Volume I (Areas 1-10)
NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.author: Timothy W. Layton, Daisy Chinburg, Ashley Braquet, Margie Coffin Brown (Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, National Park Service, Boston)
NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.from: PDF p. 3 (title page: Battlefield Rehabilitation Framework; Record of Treatment; Timothy W. Layton, Daisy Chinburg, Ashley Braquet, Margie Coffin Brown; Olmsted Center for Landscape Preservation, National Park Service, Boston, Massachusetts, 2018)
NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.text_quality: two-column report: quotes are cut from the content-stream-order text (<ID>.raw.txt, pdftotext -raw, line-end hyphenation repaired). The text layer lost the i of every fi ligature and one f of ff (feld, fre, fght, beneft), so quotes are typed in the corrected spelling and matched letter for letter with those groups ignored (quote_mode cleaned; the raw excerpt is stored next to the quote)
NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.state_dates_note: Record of Treatment: each area section gives (1) the 1863 landscape (battle-period fields, fences, orchards, woodlots, buildings, hospital use; taken from the 1863 property research and damage claims) and (2) the treatment actually carried out 1998-2013 (fences rebuilt, orchards replanted, woods cleared, non-historic features removed). Only the 1863 paragraphs describe 1863; the treatment paragraphs and the 2013-2016 photographs describe REBUILT or REPLANTED features: never an 1863 profile.
NPS-CLR-ROT-V1.covers: Battlefield Rehabilitation Framework (GMP 1999 and the 2004 Treatment Philosophy: The 1863 Landscape) and the record of treatment of the park areas by farm and field: fences, orchards, woodlots, fields, buildings, wells and springs, farm lanes
